dos.text: Begin learning with Tawheed it is the first obligation upon every human.
Understand Tawheed in its three categories.
Purify your intentions for Allāh alone in all acts of worship.
Learn the correct Names and Attributes of Allāh as revealed.
Teach Tawheed to your family with wisdom.

donts.text: Don't associate any partner with Allāh in worship this is Shirk.
Don't compare Allāh to His creation in His Attributes.
Don't seek help, protection, or blessings from other than Allāh.
Don't make intermediaries between yourself and Allāh.
Don't neglect learning Tawheed while focusing only on secondary matters.

dos.text: Internalize that true Īmān increases with obedience and decreases with sin.
Reflect on the names and attributes of Allāh to strengthen your first pillar of faith.
Send prayers (ṣalāh) upon the Prophet ﷺ daily, affirming belief in messengers.
Remember death and the Hereafter frequently to align your actions.
Trust in Allāh’s decree while taking the lawful means (asbāb) for your affairs.

donts.text: Don't deny any part of the six articles of faith; doing so nullifies Īmān.
Don't speak about the how of Allāh’s attributes (e.g., How is His Hand?); affirm them without distortion.
Don't disrespect any prophet or angel; they are all honoured servants of Allāh.
Don't fall into despair or anxiety by misunderstanding Divine Decree; it includes both good and bad as a test.
Don't  neglect the worldly life out of belief in the Hereafter; Islam commands balance.

dos.text: Learn the conditions and integrals (arkān) of each pillar.
Perform ṣalāh with congregation (jamā'ah) when possible.
Calculate zakāh accurately and give it promptly.
Protect your fast from vain speech and arguments.
Sincerely intend to perform Hajj when capable.

donts.text: Don't delay prayers beyond their prescribed times without valid excuse.
Don't treat zakāh as a mere tax; give with the intention of purification.
Don't break your fast intentionally without a Shar'ī excuse.
Don't perform Hajj with harām (unlawful) money.
Don't neglect the inner dimensions; avoid praying without humility or fasting without restraint.

dos.text: Seek refuge from Shayṭān and begin with Bismillāh before recitation.
Strive to understand the meaning, even if just one verse a day.
Maintain ritual purity (Wuḍūʾ) when touching the physical Muṣḥaf.
Listen attentively and be silent when the Qur'an is recited. "So when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy." (Al-Aʿrāf 7:204)
Let the Qur'an guide your decisions, character, and worldview.

donts.text: Don't touch the Muṣḥaf without Wuḍūʾ. "None should touch it except the purified." (Al-Wāqiʿah 56:79 - interpreted by scholars as physical purity).
Don't recite it in impure places like bathrooms.
Don't argue or be prideful with the Qur'an; its purpose is guidance, not dispute.
Don't neglect its memorization and revision if you have memorized any part. The Prophet ﷺ said it escapes the heart faster than a tied camel. (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5032)
Don't interpret it based on personal opinion; refer to the explanations of the Prophet ﷺ, his companions, and trusted scholars.

dos.text: Believe in his prophethood firmly and follow his Sunnah meticulously.

Send prayers (Ṣalāt) and peace (Salām) upon him whenever he is mentioned. "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace." (Al-Ahzab 33:56)

Love him more than yourself, your family, and your wealth. The Prophet ﷺ said: "None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his children, his parents, and all people." (Sahih al-Bukhari 15)
Study his Seerah to understand how to implement Islam in daily life.
Defend his honor and respond to slanders with wisdom and correct knowledge.

donts.text: Avoid exceeding proper bounds in praising him; he is a human servant of Allah, not divine.
Avoid depicting him in images or drawings, as this can lead to exaggeration and is prohibited.
Verify any teaching or practice attributed to him before following it.
Avoid innovating in matters of religion claiming it honors him; the best honor is following his authentic Sunnah.
Never prioritize cultural customs over his clear teachings and example.

dos.text: Plan your day around the five prayer windows
Perfect your wudu with mindfulness
Learn the meaning of what you recite in salah
Add a short sunnah prayer to deepen khushu
Pray in congregation when you can

donts.text: Don't delay fajr unless absolutely necessary
Don't think prayer is optional when you miss one
Don't rush through sujud without presence
Don't let fatigue become an excuse to skip a prayer
Don't neglect dua after prayer; cling to it

dos.text: Make duʿāʾ with humility, hope, and fear, lowering your voice between a whisper and speaking aloud.
Face the Qiblah if possible when making duʿāʾ, as the Prophet ﷺ did during important supplications. (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3995)
Use the comprehensive duʿāʾs taught by the Prophet ﷺ, such as: "Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanatan wa fil-ākhirati ḥasanatan wa qinā ʿadhāban-nār." (Al-Baqarah 2:201)
Persist in your duʿāʾ and do not say "I prayed but wasn't answered." The response is guaranteed in one of the three ways mentioned.
Make duʿāʾ for other believers in their absence, as the angels say "Āmīn, and for you the same." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2732)

donts.text: Don't be impatient or give up on duʿāʾ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The duʿāʾ of any one of you will be answered so long as he is not impatient and says, 'I made duʿāʾ but it was not answered.'" (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6340)
Don't wish for hardship to strike just so you can make duʿāʾ. Ask for well-being.
Don't supplicate for something sinful or for severing family ties.
Don't neglect dhikr in gatherings. The Prophet ﷺ warned that a gathering without dhikr of Allah is a cause for regret on Judgment Day. (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4855)
Don't use fabricated or weak duʿāʾs. Stick to what is verified in the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah.

dos.text: Start each day with morning adhkār and end with evening adhkār for protection.
Regularly recite Sūrah al-Falaq & an-Nās to cure jealousy and evil eye.
Keep company with the righteous they reflect purity onto your heart.
Perform voluntary night prayer (Tahajjud) it illuminates the heart.
Give regular charity secretly it extinguishes Allah’s anger and purifies wealth.

donts.text: Don't let a day pass without seeking forgiveness (Istighfār 100 times).
Don't backbite or listen to gossip it blackens the heart.
Don't harbor hatred for more than three days; reconcile immediately.
Don't let worldly pursuits distract you from the five daily prayers.
Don't envy others; say "Mā shāʾ Allāh" and make duʿāʾ for them and yourself.

dos.text: Say Bismillāh before every action (eating, drinking, entering home).
Use the right hand for eating, drinking, giving, and taking.
Ask permission three times before entering (Qur'an 24:27-28).
Visit the sick it's a right of one Muslim over another.
Cover sneezes and say Alḥamdulillāh; others should reply Yarḥamuk Allāh.

donts.text: Don't yawn without covering your mouth (it's from Shayṭān).
Don't backbite or listen to gossip it's like eating a brother's flesh.
Don't interrupt others while speaking.
Don't waste food or water even during ablution.
Don't laugh excessively it deadens the heart.

dos.text: Choose halal food intentionally and thank Allah
Design a bedtime routine rooted in dhikr
Keep finances transparent and honest
Blend learning with leisure to refresh your heart
Use technology to connect with beneficial circles

donts.text: Don't consume media that drains your spirit
Avoid hoarding wealth at the expense of charity
Don't rush through meals; eat with gratitude
Avoid neglecting physical rest when you need it
Don't let trends redefine your modesty

dos.text: Consult with family when making major decisions
Pray together to build spiritual closeness
Teach children salah and dua by modeling them
Speak respectfully even during disagreements
Celebrate milestones with gratitude as a household

donts.text: Don't neglect parents while raising your own family
Avoid forcing opinions without listening
Don't break promises honored in the home
Avoid rushing into marriage without istikhara
Don't allow anger to fester before reconciliation

dos.text: Volunteer for mosque events and outreach
Reach out to newcomers and make introductions
Share beneficial knowledge during gatherings
Pray behind knowledgeable imams when possible
Support neighbors with gifts or kind words

donts.text: Don't isolate yourself during key celebrations
Avoid judging others for different levels of practice
Don't withhold help when someone asks
Avoid spreading division or unfounded rumors
Don't ignore the elderly or the disabled in your circle

dos.text: Set spiritual goals rooted in Quranic guidance
Pair planning with regular dua for success
Schedule weekly check-ins with a mentor
Document small victories for motivation
Invest time in beneficial knowledge for tomorrow

donts.text: Don't live only for tomorrow and forget today
Avoid planning without taking action
Don't let disappointment halt your progress
Avoid ignoring signs that a path is harmful
Don't rely solely on luck; work and pray

dos.text: Remember Allah's mercy and justice daily
Perform sincere repentance often
Give charity with the intention of ongoing reward
Check your deeds each night before sleeping
Teach loved ones about accountability gently

donts.text: Don't dismiss the grave and Day of Judgment
Avoid delaying repentance because of shame
Don't take your wealth for granted
Avoid hoarding deeds without consistency
Don't let fear freeze you into inaction

dos.text: Reflect on descriptions of paradise to spark hope
Practice gratitude to taste paradise on earth
Speak kindly to earn Allah's mercy
Repent before you sleep each night
Share stories of the hereafter with children

donts.text: Don't ignore warnings about sinful paths
Avoid assuming you are guaranteed paradise
Don't become hardened toward those who sin
Avoid using fear to portray Allah as distant
Don't trivialize the importance of repentance
